title: Sarita Instrument Artisan [cite: 108]
summary_statement: Visionary innovators who redefined the Philippine Rondalla by mastering the use of engineered bamboo for professional-grade string instruments. [cite: 112]
full_content: Jay Sarita, director of the Dipolog Community Rondalla, has dedicated his entire career to the advancement of rondalla music. [cite: 113]
Through his workshop, Sarita Instrument Artisan, he has earned a reputation as one of the most reliable instrument makers in the Philippines. [cite: 114]
His most significant contribution to the Philippine creative industry is reinventing rondalla instruments — traditionally made from expensive hardwoods — crafted entirely from bamboo. [cite: 115]
His work bridges the gap between traditional folk instrumentation and modern professional standards. [cite: 116]
The Sarita workshop produces a full range of ensemble instruments, including the Banduria, Octavina, Laud, Guitar, Mandola, Piccolo Banduria, Double Bass, and even ukuleles. [cite: 117]
Their bamboo Marimbas are unique, featuring bamboo tone scales and metal tube resonators to achieve precise tuning across three or three-and-a-half octaves. [cite: 118]
These instruments are built for high-level performance, not display, and are used by the Dipolog Community Rondalla to showcase the world-class potential of Philippine bamboo. [cite: 119]
Sarita's technical approach relies on engineered bamboo and specific species like Gigantochloa levis (Bolo) for his Angklung sets. [cite: 120]

Unlike traditional IP instruments that use raw culms, Sarita uses laminated and engineered bamboo to keep complex string instruments like the Banduria and Octavina stable and resonant under high string tension. [cite: 121]
For his Angklung, he attaches G. levis tubes to an engineered bamboo frame, creating an instrument that is both ecologically sustainable and durable enough for international use. [cite: 122]

quote.text: "Bamboo is the key to making the Filipino Rondalla sustainable and accessible to every student in the country." [cite: 123]
